mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to a decrease in S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where FEDFUNDS increased by more than 0.25% in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3 percentage points in a month signals a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to an increase in S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as consumer spending and business confidence rise.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where UNRATE decreased by more than 0.3pp in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a strong demand environment, which typically leads to an increase in S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings grow.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in more than 40% of the quarters where GDPC1 increased over the previous two quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month signals a weakening supply side, which typically leads to a decrease in S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as economic output slows and uncertainty rises.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where INDPRO decreased by more than 1% in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals an inflationary environment with tight monetary policy, which typically leads to a decrease in S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as real returns are eroded.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
regime_hint: inflationary period with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where FEDFUNDS was above 4% and CPIAUCSL increased by more than 0.5% in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month, it signals a tight labor market with strong job growth, which typically leads to an increase in S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as consumer spending and business investment rise.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS increases > 200,000 in 1 month
regime_hint: full employment with strong job growth
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where UNRATE was below 4% and PAYEMS increased by more than 200,000 in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over two consecutive months signals a strong demand in the housing market, which typically leads to an increase in S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as the broader economy benefits from increased construction activity and related sectors.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in more than 40% of the months where HOUST increased over the previous two months.

mechanism_narrative: When the industrial production index (INDPRO) is below its 12-month moving average and the real GDP (GDPC1) decreases for two consecutive quarters, it signals a weakening supply side with a slowing economy, which typically leads to a decrease in S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings decline.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month MA and GDPC1 decreases for 2 consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the quarters where INDPRO was below its 12-month moving average and GDPC1 decreased for two consecutive quarters.
